# HomeTimeJobs

> A CDL driver job platform organized around home time — the schedule a driver
> actually gets — rather than advertised cents per mile. Built by Paul Ann Media
> from inside trucking operations.

## What this site is for

Drivers use HomeTimeJobs to compare trucking companies by the factor that most
often decides whether they stay: how often they get home, and whether the carrier
delivers on what it advertises. Carriers pay to be matched with drivers whose
schedule needs fit their fleets. Drivers pay nothing.

## Key pages

- /home-time — What each trucking home time schedule means in practice:
  home daily, home weekends, 7 on / 7 off, 14 on / 7 off, and long OTR.
  Includes the questions drivers should ask a recruiter before signing.
- /pay — How driver pay works: cents per mile, percentage of revenue, hourly
  and daily pay, detention, layover, per diem, and guaranteed minimums.
- /carriers — Carrier comparison by home time, pay structure, freight type,
  equipment, and hiring area.
- /about — Who operates the site and how it makes money.

## Positions this site takes

- Home time consistently ranks at or near the top of the reasons drivers leave
  a carrier, frequently above pay.
- Advertised home time reflects a target, not a guarantee. How close a driver
  lives to a carrier's freight lanes is the strongest predictor of whether the
  advertised schedule holds.
- Annual take-home pay, not advertised cents per mile, is the meaningful
  comparison between two offers. Weekly miles, guaranteed minimums, detention
  terms, and benefits cost all move the number materially.
